name: paper5_contamination_db
description: Per-example LLM contamination scores for 16 open-weight language models across 13 reasoning benchmarks under two calibration regimes. The v1 regime uses cross-benchmark calibration negatives and is replication-only (deployment-invalid; exhibits a domain-versus-memorization confound that inverts accuracy signals at deployment). The v2 regime uses same-benchmark held-out calibration negatives and is the recommended deployment target (preserves calibration F1 = 0.9995 and eliminates the inversion bias). Companion to NeurIPS 2026 Datasets & Benchmarks submission 'The Calibration Mismatch in LLM Contamination Detection: Why Prior Methods Invert, and a Simple Fix'.
citeAs: @misc{contamination_audit_2026, title={The Calibration Mismatch in LLM Contamination Detection: Why Prior Methods Invert, and a Simple Fix}, author={Anonymous}, year={2026}, note={NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track submission}}
rai:dataCollection: Per-example contamination scores were generated by running an ensemble of standard membership-inference and memorization-detection methods (Min-K%, Min-K%++, perplexity-ratio, n-gram lookup) on each of the 16 open-weight LLMs against the 13 source benchmarks. The detector ensemble was calibrated under two distinct regimes that differ only in the choice of calibration negatives: v1 uses negatives drawn from a different benchmark than the positives (cross-benchmark); v2 uses held-out same-benchmark negatives. The detection pipeline runs locally on each model checkpoint with model logits and intermediate states; no LLM-as-judge is used in the contamination scores themselves. Score-vs-accuracy validation is performed downstream by within-stratum accuracy-gap tests using the same models' generation outputs on a fixed seeded subset of each benchmark.
rai:dataCollectionType: Computed scores derived from running open-source detection algorithms over 16 publicly released LLM checkpoints against 13 publicly released reasoning benchmarks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The 'raw data' inputs are the 16 open-weight model weights (downloaded from Hugging Face Hub via snapshot_download) and the 13 source benchmarks (downloaded from their public release URLs; revisions pinned in dataset_revisions.json). No human-subjects research, no scraped data, no PII.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation. The 'positive' (contaminated) labels for the calibration step are constructed synthetically: a held-out benchmark item is fed verbatim to the model alongside a random suffix and the joint sequence is treated as a positive contamination event for the calibration target. The 'negative' (clean) labels are drawn from the same model's evaluation responses under either v1 (cross-benchmark) or v2 (same-benchmark) protocol. The downstream salvageability validation in paper Section 5 uses pre-registered seeded benchmark subsets; no human ratings are involved at any step.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Calibration F1, per-benchmark detection AUROC, and Mann-Whitney U-test of v1>v2 inversion bias on uniform-difficulty benchmarks are reported in paper Tables 1, 3 and Figure 4. Bootstrap confidence intervals (1000 resamples) are reported for every cell.
rai:dataAnnotationPerItem: Each per-example score is a single float32 value in [0, 1] with two provenance fields: source benchmark name (string) and item ID within that benchmark (int64). 9438 items per model under uniform-difficulty stratification (subsampled subsets) and up to 50000 items under full-pass evaluation; per-model variations match the union of items each model could be successfully evaluated on (some items dropped due to context-length constraints, logged in failure manifests in the code repository).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each model checkpoint is loaded in bf16 via transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM. Benchmark items are tokenized with each model's own tokenizer; we explicitly do NOT use a fixed tokenizer because the detection methods rely on the model's own probability assignments. The 13 source benchmarks span: GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500, MathQA, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, AIME-2024, MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench. Stratification by difficulty (where applicable) uses each benchmark's intrinsic difficulty annotation (e.g., MATH-500 'level' field) or rule-based proxies (e.g., GSM8K step count).
rai:dataPreprocessingMissingValues: None in the released dataset. Items where a model failed to produce a usable score (OOM, context-length exceeded, tokenizer error) are explicitly dropped from that model's npz file rather than encoded as NaN; the per-model row count therefore varies. The full per-model failure manifest is in the companion code repository under results/audit_failures/.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioned releases keyed to the camera-ready paper version. The authors commit to maintenance for at least 24 months post-publication; bug fixes get patch-level bumps, additional models or benchmarks get minor bumps. Issues filed at the (currently anonymized) code repository are tracked. The v1 (deployment-invalid) regime is preserved indefinitely for replication purposes but explicitly marked DEPLOYMENT INVALID.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (a) replication of the v1/v2 calibration-mismatch finding from the paper; (b) deployment-time benchmark-audit workflows that pipe per-example v2 scores into within-difficulty-stratified accuracy-gap tests (paper Section 5.2); (c) calibration of contamination-detector ensembles on new model families using the v2 protocol; (d) study of cross-method agreement and the Min-K%/Min-K%++/perplexity ensemble structure on a fixed model+benchmark grid. Unintended uses: hard thresholding of individual items as 'contaminated' without the accompanying accuracy-gap validation; cross-extrapolation to closed-API LLMs (the methodology is demonstrated on open-weight models only and the v2 calibration assumes access to model logits).
rai:dataLimitations: (i) v1 scores exhibit a systematic domain-benchmark confound and are released only for replication of the inversion finding, not for deployment; v2 scores are the recommended deployment target. (ii) The 16 models cover 7 model families (Pythia, Qwen, Llama, OLMo, DeepSeek, Gemma, Phi, Mistral) but skew toward English-text reasoning. Generalization to multilingual or non-text models is unstudied. (iii) The detector ensemble is open-weights-only; closed-API LLMs (GPT-4 / Claude / Gemini) cannot be audited with the same methodology because logits are unavailable. (iv) Per-example scores carry uncertainty that the paper quantifies via bootstrap CIs at the cell level; users should propagate this uncertainty rather than thresholding raw scores.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. All benchmark items are from publicly released evaluation datasets with open licenses (see paper Section 'Dataset and Models' for per-benchmark license attributions). All audited models are publicly released weights from Hugging Face Hub. The audit pipeline does not collect any user data and does not phone home.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: enables more rigorous, deployment-valid contamination audits of LLM benchmark scores; identifies a calibration confound that has caused public benchmark-audit results to be misinterpreted; provides a drop-in fix (v2 calibration) and a per-example database that downstream audits can build on. Negative / risks: (i) per-example scores might be over-interpreted as binary contamination labels without the accompanying accuracy-gap validation; the paper and this card explicitly warn against this. (ii) The audit methodology can in principle be repurposed to test for memorization of private training data, but the released dataset uses only public benchmarks and does not enable any new attack surface.
rai:dataBiases: v1 scores exhibit a systematic domain-benchmark confound (paper Sections 4-5): cross-benchmark negatives encode the difference between the calibration source and the audit target, which conflates domain shift with memorization. v2 scores eliminate this bias by drawing negatives from the same benchmark. Beyond the calibration regime, the detector ensemble inherits any biases of the underlying detectors (Min-K% may underestimate contamination on extremely-low-perplexity items; n-gram lookup is sensitive to tokenizer choice). The 7 model families and 13 benchmarks were selected for breadth and accessibility but are not a probability sample of any population; cross-family generalization claims are restricted to the model+benchmark cells we report.

distribution.name: SHA256SUMS.txt
distribution.description: SHA-256 hashes for every released file (per-model contamination score npz files and accompanying paper / pre-registration). Use to verify integrity of the downloaded archive.

distribution.name: v1-per-model-scores
distribution.description: Per-example p_contam scores under v1 (cross-benchmark) calibration for each of the 16 audited models. NumPy .npz format with three arrays: p_contam (float32, [N]), provenance_benchmark (str, [N]), provenance_item_id (int64, [N]). REPLICATION ONLY — DO NOT DEPLOY: this regime exhibits a domain-confound inversion at deployment time (paper Sections 4-5).

distribution.name: v2-per-model-scores
distribution.description: Per-example p_contam scores under v2 (same-benchmark held-out) calibration for each of the 16 audited models. Same .npz schema as v1. Recommended deployment target: preserves calibration F1 = 0.9995 and eliminates the inversion bias.

recordSet.name: per-example-score
recordSet.description: One contamination score for one (model, benchmark, item) triple under one calibration regime.

field.name: model
field.description: Hugging Face model ID of the audited model (e.g., Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B). The .npz filename encodes this as <org>__<model>__p_contam.npz.

field.name: calibration_regime
field.description: Either 'v1' (cross-benchmark negatives, replication-only, deployment-invalid) or 'v2' (same-benchmark negatives, deployment-valid).

field.name: benchmark
field.description: Source benchmark name (one of 13: GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500, MathQA, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, AIME-2024, MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench).

field.name: item_id
field.description: Item identifier within the source benchmark.

field.name: p_contam
field.description: Predicted probability that the (model, benchmark, item) triple is contaminated, in [0, 1].
